text:
The evidence can't say whether the loss violates forest protection rules. It shows what changed, not whether it was legal.

**What it shows:** Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022 on the 17.6 ha property (3.41% of the area). The JRC 2020 reference agrees that the affected area was forest, and a later year (up to 2025) was observed, so the loss is corroborated. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 0.5 ha of it as native forest and 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest. A further 0.2 ha of loss in small patches was not counted as an event.

**What it doesn't establish:** Whether deforestation or land-use change occurred, since Hansen loss covers any stand replacement. It also doesn't establish the cause, whether the change was authorized or illegal, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.

A rules assessment would need permit records, the cause of the loss, and the applicable native forest regulations.
